thread:
ida_support: heads up — customer PhiLabs hit a burst of embed insert rejects right after we flipped the quantized 1536->1024 variant yesterday. They started seeing 400s from the indexer and large backlog on our backfill queue.

sam_eng: copy, any error snippets?

ida_support: yes — indexer rejects with `schema_mismatch: vector_dim=1536 expected but got 1024` for ~12% of inserts. We saw it after the model swap at 22:03 UTC; some producers still sending old-variant vectors. Backfill started at 22:10 and created a heap of 429 responses from vecdb.

lee_ml: so a mixed-dim situation — how did that happen? I thought the quantized rollout included a conversion layer.

ida_support: rollout note said fallback allowed both variants for 24h. Looks like clients didn't rotate; some internal backfill workers are pulling older model and re-ingesting older dim vectors.

noah_ops: logs from the indexer: ```ERROR IndexInsert failed id=phl_87321 code=VECTOR_DIM_MISMATCH expected=1536 got=1024 trace=ingest/worker.go:412```

ida_support: customer impact: ~15% of new docs rejected, search recall affected, billing spike for retries (they're concerned). CSM Ana is on the thread.

csm_ana: PhiLabs is asking for ETA on fix and whether data was lost. They need a short summary and mitigation ASAP.

sam_eng: immediate triage — can we short-circuit the backfill? throttle or pause it while we sort dims. Who controls the backfill queue?

noah_ops: I can pause the backfill workers for the PhiLabs tenant. That will stop new rejects and give us time.

ida_support: thank you. Please pause and confirm.

noah_ops: paused at 22:35 UTC. :white_check_mark:

lee_ml: remediation options: 1) convert 1024 -> 1536 by re-embedding with current model (accurate but slow backfill), 2) keep both dims and route 1024 docs to a compatible vecdb table (schema split), 3) revert rollout to only 1536 variant if feasible. Thoughts?

sam_eng: Option 2 sounds safest short-term: create a temporary index/table that accepts 1024 vectors for PhiLabs and keep queries fallback aware. Lower risk than re-embedding millions.

ida_support: customer wants minimal service disruption. Option 2 + scheduled backfill of older docs to new dim seems reasonable. Need ops + eng to estimate time.

noah_ops: I can spin up a compat index. ETA ~ 45min to provision and wire tenant routing. We'll set a TTL and plan a later cleanup.

sam_eng: while that's happening I'll add a filter at the ingest proxy to detect dim != 1536 and mark route=compat-table for PhiLabs. Patch in staging now, pushing to prod after quick smoke.

deploy-bot: deploy queued by sam_eng: "ingest-dim-router-patch" to prod.

ida_support: also need a communication blurb for customer: short explanation, mitigation, and whether data lost. CSM Ana can draft but include exact numbers. Sam/noah — can you confirm counts?

noah_ops: current stats in the window 22:03-22:34 UTC: attempted inserts 87,942; rejected 13,582 (~15.4%). I saved sample ids.

lee_ml: for long-term, we should disallow dual-dim in rollouts or auto-normalize via on-the-fly re-embed in the ingest proxy. I'll file an RFC.

sam_eng: quick repro steps added to thread: \n1) run a client that requests embeddings with old quantized model (1024).\n2) send a batch to /v1/embeddings (our tenant key) while indexer expects 1536.\n3) observe indexer errors and backfill rejects.

ida_support: sample curl (for support run):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <PHILABS_KEY>" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"model":"embed-quant-old","input":["doc A","doc B"]}'
```

noah_ops: compatibility index provisioned and wired at 23:12 UTC. Routing patch applied at 23:18 UTC. Rejection rate dropped to <1% for new inserts. :tada:

csm_ana: I'll send PhiLabs the mitigation note and the numbers. They asked for timeline on normalized state.

sam_eng: for normalization/backfill plan: schedule a controlled backfill to re-embed the 13.5k rejected docs with the current model, rate-limited to avoid overload. Estimate ~3 hours total with current fleet, or we can expedite with dedicated capacity for a day.

ida_support: customer asked about billing refunds for failed inserts. @finance-lead can weigh in but we should offer credit for the rejects while we did mitigation.

lee_ml: filing RFC: "prevent dual-dim rollouts + auto-normalize path" assigned to me.

noah_ops: marking this incident resolved for immediate customer impact — metric shows health restored. We'll keep the compat index live until backfill done.

ida_support: thanks team. Next steps summarized for CSM: paused backfill, compat index up, routing patch live, re-embed backfill scheduled, RFC initiated. I'll close the ticket when backfill completes. :memo:
